summary.name: Digital preservation
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article explaining digital preservation, the formal practice of keeping digital information of continuing value accessible and usable over the long term.
keywords: how to preserve digital files long term
use_cases: understanding long-term access to digital records
planning a digital archive or library repository
choosing file formats for long-term storage
verifying files have not changed using checksums
learning about OAIS and PREMIS standards
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia overview of digital preservation rather than a software tool. It defines the field and its core concepts: appraisal, identification and metadata, integrity, fixity and checksums, characterization, sustainability, and authenticity. It covers format and physical media obsolescence and the significant properties of digital objects. It also summarizes standards and history, including the 1996 RLG/CPA task force report, the OAIS reference model (published 2012), the Trusted Digital Repository model, and the InterPARES project.
notable: Covers OAIS, PREMIS, and Trusted Digital Repository standards
Explains fixity, checksums, and file attendance
Discusses short lifespans of hard drives, flash memory, optical discs, and LTO tapes
Describes the challenge of preserving software without source code
caveats: Describes concepts and history, not a software tool; the awesome-selfhosted listing is for digital archiving software
